topics.title: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle: Polynesia and the language of animals
topics.ncert_sections: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Part I

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the Cat's-food-Man and Polynesia advise Doctor Dolittle to become an animal doctor.
Describe how, according to Polynesia, animals and birds communicate with one another.

topics.title: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle: the plough horse and the Doctor's fame
topics.ncert_sections: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Part II

concepts.learning_objective: Recount the plough horse's problem and explain how speaking its language helped the Doctor cure it.
Explain how Doctor Dolittle cared for many kinds of animals and how his fame spread across the world.

topics.title: Dr. Dolittle: compound words, palindromes and the present perfect tense
topics.ncert_sections: Animals, Birds, and Dr. Dolittle, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Classify compound words from the story as hyphenated, open or closed compounds.
Identify words and sentences that read the same backwards as forwards.
Use the present perfect tense (has/have + past participle) for actions relevant at the time of speaking.

topics.title: A Funny Man: the poem and its humour

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the odd actions of the funny man and the poet's reactions to them.
Identify devices such as alliteration, rhyme and mixed-up sense images that create humour in the poem.

topics.title: A Funny Man: phrasal verbs and limericks
topics.ncert_sections: A Funny Man, Let us learn and Let us write

concepts.learning_objective: Use phrasal verbs such as take up, take after, take in, take over and take off with their correct meanings.
Recognise the five-line form and AABBA rhyme scheme of a limerick.

topics.title: Say the Right Thing: Mrs. Shaw's advice (Scene I)
topics.ncert_sections: Say the Right Thing, Scene I

concepts.learning_objective: Recall the advice Mrs. Shaw gives Mary about polite conversation with guests.
Infer Mary's character from her confident replies to her mother in Scene I.

topics.title: Say the Right Thing: Mary's blunders (Scene II)
topics.ncert_sections: Say the Right Thing, Scene II

concepts.learning_objective: Identify how each of Mary's remarks unknowingly offends Mrs. Harding or Mrs. Lee.
Explain how stage directions and the final line create humour in the play.

topics.title: Say the Right Thing: suffixes, tenses and kinds of sentences
topics.ncert_sections: Say the Right Thing, Let us learn

concepts.learning_objective: Form and analyse words using suffixes such as -ous, -ly, -ful, -ance and -est.
Use the present perfect continuous tense (has/have + been + verb-ing) for actions continuing up to now.
Identify declarative, interrogative, exclamatory and imperative sentences and punctuate them correctly.
